transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-12 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~45 min
Attendees: Maya Torres (Redwood AE), Ravi Kapoor (Redwood SE), Lena Kim (Redwood SE), Olivia Chen (Ember Digital - Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Ember - Infra), Priya Singh (Ember - PM), Ethan Brooks (Ember - SRE)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping to align on integration approach (OpenAI-compatible endpoints + SDKs), define success criteria (latency/accuracy/cost), agree on workload sizing and benchmark plan, and set timeline for a 2-3 week pilot.

Topics:
- Integration: OpenAI-compat endpoints, SDK examples, function/tool-calling, structured JSON outputs
- Workloads: QPS, tokens/request, concurrency, caching expectations
- Benchmarks: throughput, p95/p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, failure modes
- Security & networking: VPC/private deployment options, KMS, audit logs
- Timeline & next steps for pilot

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): thanks everyone for joining, quick intro from our side, im maya, im the account lead, ravi and lena are going to cover technicals
[00:12] Olivia (Ember): hi all, thanks, im olivia, we run the ML platform, priya will speak to product goals, marcus on infra and ethan on reliability
[00:30] Maya: cool, objective for today is to decide how we integrate—do we use Redwood hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints or a private deploy, and what does the POC look like
[00:45] Ravi (Redwood): quick note — we support an OpenAI-compatible REST + SDK surface, function/tool calling and structured output; streaming is supported too. For POCs we usually run a small benchmark harness to validate latency and throughput on customer sample payloads
[01:10] Marcus (Ember): for context, our peak production loads today are around 120 qps for search fallbacks, avg tokens per request ~650, bursts to 350 qps for 10-15 minutes during campaigns; we care about p95/p99 latency for user-facing flows, and cost is a big part of success criteria
[01:40] Priya (Ember): product goal is to add a smart summarization + cite tool inside our analytics UI — success means 95% of calls return within 600ms and summaries meet our accuracy bar on a 50-case eval set, also total inference cost not to exceed $0.05 per call at target traffic
[02:05] Ravi: noted — typical Redwood hosted p95s depend on model selection and batch config; for transformer-based open models we often see p95 around 200-400ms for short responses but with larger token footprints it changes. If latency SLO is 600ms we have multiple knobs: dedicated capacity, smaller model + reranker, and prefix caching
[02:40] Ethan (Ember): nv, for SRE perspective, we need to know network egress and whether we can peer VPCs, or do a Private (VPC) deployment; also audit logs and KMS are mandatory for compliance
[03:05] Lena (Redwood): we have both options — hosted with enterprise tenancy + VPC peering or Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC); we support KMS integrations and detailed audit logs. we'll include SOC2 evidence in the security pack.
[03:30] Olivia: good. on integration — we already have some code using OpenAI APIs. how close is your compatibility? can we swap endpoints with minimal changes?
[03:50] Ravi: yes, designed to be drop-in compatible for common endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings). we also extend function calling semantics and structured output. we can share SDK snippets in node/python and a migration diff to demonstrate minimal changes
[04:15] Priya: we also need structured JSON outputs for the summarizer (title, bullets[], citations[]). how do you validate and constrain structure?
[04:30] Lena: we recommend using function-calling spec to enforce schema; Redwood supports model-side function calling and we surface model responses as parsed JSON. For safety we add a schema validator in the SDK and a heuristic fallback if the model returns malformed JSON
[04:55] Marcus: benchmark question — we want both latency and cost numbers. what does a typical POC bench look like?
[05:10] Ravi: plan: 3-day bench. Day 1: baseline single-instance p95/p99 for your sample prompts at 1-10 qps. Day 2: throughput ramp to target qps (120->350 qps) capturing p95/p99 and CPU/GPU utilization. Day 3: failure/injection tests, function-calling runs, and cost estimation by simulating typical token lengths. We'll run the harness against Redwood hosted and optionally a Private deployment if you want parity numbers
[05:50] Olivia: sounds reasonable — can you simulate prefix caching and batching like you'd see in prod?
[06:00] Ravi: yes, test harness includes KV/prefix caching scenarios; we can run both with and without caching to show impact on latency and cost. we'll also include batching configs that mimic your traffic shape
[06:20] Priya: timeline — how long for integration engineering work? we have a sprint in 2 weeks and want a pilot in the following sprint
[06:31] Maya: typical POC timeline: week 0 (this week) alignment and security paperwork, week 1: SDK integration + sample run, week 2: benchmark runs, week 3: iterate on model config and SLO tuning, by end of week 3 we aim to have pilot results and a go/no-go with a SOW to move to dedicated capacity if needed
[06:55] Ethan: for network — do you require an outbound connection for hosted? or can everything be internal with Private?
[07:05] Lena: hosted is outbound to Redwood endpoints; for full isolation we recommend Redwood Private which runs in your VPC or on-prem with no outbound to public internet. for PCI/regulated data we've seen customers prefer Private
[07:22] Marcus: cost control question — is there a way to route low-latency high-cost traffic to cheaper variants? e.g., route embeddings to cheaper quantized model and keep interactive flows on faster ones
[07:40] Ravi: yes, smart routing and model variants are supported — per-route policies can route by latency priority or cost priority and fallback to smaller quantized variants. Redwood Optimize can also recommend quantization profiles per workload
[07:58] Olivia: we'd like to validate function calling for structured citations — specifically we need deterministic citation fields and model hallucinations are a no-go. how is that handled?
[08:15] Lena: function calling plus post-parse validation and an external citation verification step (simple retrieval & score) in the pipeline is the recommended approach. for the POC we can add a lightweight retrieval check to measure false citation rate
[08:40] Priya: success criteria recap — latency p95 < 600ms (ideally < 400ms), cost < $0.05 per call at target traffic, accuracy: summaries meet internal eval on 50-case set (we'll provide prompts). if these are met, we proceed to a dedicated pilot.
[09:05] Maya: I'll draft a success criteria doc and SOW; ravi will own the benchmark harness and lena will attach security docs.
[09:20] Olivia: what about SDKs — node/python examples and service-side streaming?
[09:30] Ravi: we'll share open-source SDK snippets and a small express/node wrapper that mirrors OpenAI's responses including streaming and function-calling examples. also python example for synchronous flows and a small test runner to replay your prompts
[09:50] Marcus: on observability — we need per-route latency breakdown, token-cost attribution, and trace context forwarded to our traces. can we get those?
[10:05] Lena: yes, Redwood Console exposes per-route token & latency breakdown, and we support trace hooks (we pass trace IDs and can integrate with your tracing backend). we'll include sample dashboards in the security pack
[10:25] Priya: any blockers on our side? we need to prepare a subset of data to test and confirm legal for PII handling; also we may need an NDA for security docs
[10:40] Maya: we can run under a temp NDA and we'll include a limited data-handling addendum; for PII we recommend anonymized test data for initial runs, then an on-prem/private deployment test for real data
[10:55] Olivia: can we get a sample benchmark report template?
[11:05] Ravi: yes we'll provide last-run templates — p95/p99, tokens per call, cost per 1k tokens, GPU utilization, cache hit rate, and breakdown per model variant
[11:25] Maya: recap of next steps — send SDK snippets, security pack, pricing + pilot SOW, schedule bench run week of 1/18. agreed?
[11:35] All: yes

End transcript.
